title: Quick Authoring Cartridges — sketch and user stories
content:
Goal: quick, composable mini-templates (cartridges) that developers and product folks can assemble into prompts or assistant features without hand-editing full prompts every time. Think: small atomic prompt pieces (instruction + constraints + examples) that are parametric and versioned in the Console and callable from the API.

Problem / motivation:
- Teams repeatedly recreate slight variations of the same guidance (tone, safety layer, formatting).
- Large monolithic prompt files are brittle for rollouts and A/Bs.
- Want faster iterations for product teams and non-engineer authors (PMs, content designers).
- Need to expose economical composition that keeps token cost predictable (avoid duplicative instruction per turn).

Product hypothesis:
If we provide a library of tiny, composable instruction blocks with parameter substitution, authors will iterate 3x faster and engineers will reduce token duplication by ~20% via shared cartridge caching.

Personas:
- PM / Content designer: builds new assistant behaviors quickly using drag/drop cartridges in Console. Not an LLM expert.
- FE/BE engineer: integrates cartridge composition via API, pins versions, orchestrates fallbacks.
- Solutions engineer / Customer: creates curated cartridge bundles for enterprise on Redwood Private.

Core primitives (rough):
- Cartridge: small JSON/YAML snippet with fields: id, version, role (system/user/assistant), body (templated string), tokens_estimate, tags, constraints, sample_inputs (optional).
- CartridgeBundle: ordered list of cartridge ids + bundle metadata (name, owner, version, rollout policy).
- Runtime composition: server-side merge rules (prefix concatenation, param injection, de-dup heuristics).

UX sketches (Console):
- Library view: filterable by tags (tone, length, domain, safety), search by token estimate.
- Composer canvas: drag cartridges into a linear flow, toggle visibility, preview token count and sample output.
- Param panel: global and per-cartridge parameters ({{company_name}}, {{locale}}).
- Versioning panel: list of versions, diff view, rollout controls (canary %, route).

API sketches (very rough):
- POST /v1/cartridges -> create
- GET /v1/cartridges/{id}?version=x -> fetch cartridge
- POST /v1/bundles -> create bundle
- POST /v1/infer with body: {bundle_id, bundle_version, params, overrides, session_id}
  - server expands bundle into prompt and does token-aware caching when prefix identical across requests

User stories (examples):
- As a product designer, I want to build a chat flow with separate cartridges for "safety guardrail", "short-answer style", and "corporate tone" so I can toggle tone without editing the whole prompt.
- As an engineer, I want to pin cartridge versions per customer so we can safely roll forwards if a content regression happens.
- As an enterprise buyer, I want to share a private cartridge bundle across my org and control who can publish new versions.

Success metrics (candidate):
- Time-to-prototype (Console): decrease median time from idea->test from 2 days to 8 hours for small features.
- Token savings: measure % reduction in repeated instruction tokens for customers who adopt shared cartridges vs baseline. Target 15–25% in first 6 months.
- Adoption: X bundles created / weekly by PMs in pilot orgs.
- Stability: fewer content regressions (tracked by differentials in micro-evals) after version pin + rollback usage.

Constraints / non-goals:
- Not solving complex programmatic orchestration (that's a follow-up: conditional branching in bundles).
- Cartridges should be small (<= 200 tokens typical) — otherwise expose as regular model-backed templates.
- We will not expose arbitrary code execution; param templating limited to safe replacements (no eval).

Technical considerations / open infra questions:
- How to cache cartridges server-side? Likely prefix hashing + KV cache keyed by bundle fingerprint and param hash. Need eviction policy sensitive to per-customer quotas.
- Token accounting: when cartridges are merged, we need to show an accurate estimate and break down which cartridge contributes most.
- Rollbacks: must be able to retroactively run a request against previous bundle versions for debugging/eval. Storage implications.
- Compatibility with Private deployments: cartridge storage can be customer-hosted or synced to Redwood control plane depending on privacy settings.

Open UX questions / unresolved:
- Should cartridges be able to include short examples? (adds tokens but often necessary). Maybe optional, but flagged in UI as high-cost.
- Merge behavior for conflicting instructions (two cartridges both set different "style" guidance) — rules: last-wins by order in bundle, but Console should warn.
- Permissions model: who can publish to shared libraries? Approval workflow?

Edge cases to test:
- Large-scale bundles (100+ cartridges) — performance implications for runtime expansion.
- Multi-locale bundles: param injection + fallbacks.
- Function calling / tools inside cartridges: how do we handle tool specs duplication? Probably disallow tool registration in cartridges for now, instead allow bundle-level tool spec.

Next steps / immediate experiments (MVP roadmap):
1) Internals experiment: implement tiny in-memory cartridge store + bundle expansion in a dev runtime. Measure expansion time and token breakdown. (eng: serving-runtime + infra; owner: Lucien)
2) Console prototype: minimal library + drag/reorder + preview. Rapid user test with 3 PMs. (owner: Kiera)
3) API experiment: simple /infer path that accepts bundle JSON inline (no persistent storage) to validate runtime cache heuristics. (owner: Maya)
4) Pilot: 2 internal teams adopt for small support-bot features; collect token savings and iteration time.

Notes / rough timeline:
- 2-week spike for runtime prototype
- 3-week Console micro-UX
- 6-week pilot including instrumented metrics

Random brainstorming fragments (for later parsing):
- "cartridge marketplace" vs private bundles — marketplace only later
- UI: quick-swap keyboard shortcut to toggle a cartridge in preview
- Dev ergonomics: CLI tool to package cartridges from local files + upload metadata
- Editor: include inline token heatmap for cartridges

Questions for the team chat / to decide in next sync:
- QA: blocking tests for rollout safety (automated micro-eval smoke) — do we have a baseline harness? link: confluence:micro-eval-harness
- Legal: any content licensing implications for shared cartridges? ask Legal.
- Pricing: if cartridges reduce tokens, do we adjust visible pricing? maybe show estimated cost delta in Console.

Bottom line: small building blocks that make prompt authoring modular, shareable, and easier to rollout. MVP scope intentionally narrow: library + bundle composition + versioning + runtime expansion with basic caching and token accounting.

-- Lucien
